The manipulation of time in the story is very effective and well-balanced. In terms of "story time," the present-day action spans only a few minutes—Nora unlocks the door, steps into the hallway, walks into the kitchen, and looks out the window. However, the author stretches these brief moments by weaving in sharp sensory details (the creaking floorboard, the smell of scorched wool, the white button) and flashbacks. At the same time, twenty years of estrangement and childhood history are compressed into a few brief, poignant memories triggered by the empty house. This balance between the slow, quiet pacing of the present and the compressed weight of the past creates a deeply atmospheric and emotionally resonant mood.
